children: A number of stocks jumped in the morning session after specialized cloud provider CoreWeave lifted its annual sales forecast, alleviating concerns over cooling artificial intelligence hardware demand. CoreWeave said in its quarterly release that third-quarter revenue surged 168% year-over-year to $3.66 billion, while its order backlog expanded to $132.5 billion.

The company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to between $13.0 billion and $13.3 billion, ahead of the $12.9 billion consensus compiled by Reuters, and lifted capital expenditure plans to between $37 billion and $39 billion.The update alleviated credit market fears that debt-fueled data center buildouts would stall.

In research cited by CNBC, JPMorgan credit analysts noted that expanding operating cash flow and a targeted inflection to adjusted profitability in 2028 resolve immediate funding overhangs. With CoreWeave utilizing customer prepayments rather than new debt to fund expansion, hardware delivery schedules remain intact.For chipmakers, cloud capital spending directly underpins forward silicon demand. When infrastructure operators demonstrate that contracted leasing demand can fund physical deployment, it protects order books and pricing power across advanced processor and memory suppliers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Semtech’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 84 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 2 days ago when the stock gained 13.1% on the news that semiconductor and hardware shares mounted a synchronized rebound from the sharp post-election slump tied to worries over future artificial intelligence data center construction.

CNBC reported that investors reassessed that buildout once Democrats won control of Congress, and that technology shares recovered on Monday, with the S&P 500 tech sector up 2% in early trading. JPMorgan told CNBC it does not see artificial intelligence as a continued sell, and that a steadier technology tape would make the spending upcycle look more sustainable. The major indexes were up roughly 2%, so a move of 3% to 4% mostly tracks that wider rebound. The larger gains in this group sit on top of it, including double-digit moves in Monolithic Power, Semtech, and Entegris.

Semtech is up 67.5% since the beginning of the year, but at $126.03 per share, it is still trading 36.1% below its 52-week high of $197.20 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Semtech’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,397.
